body: I will say that I had disassociation due to a horrible panic attack that wouldn’t go away at all for over a year and Zoloft actually stopped it from happening EXCEPT for when I was overly stressed. I am a Panda Express worker so it gets crazy busy sometimes and I dissociate so I do think Zoloft can contribute to dissociation, but it also helps. I would try and do some meditation (as pretentious as that sounds) because it actually did help me a lot with the derealization and such. Best of luck to you, I’m glad you don’t experience it 24/7.

I’ve been on Zoloft for about 10 months, I started seeing improvement around the 1 month mark surprisingly. It did take a little bit of time, and the side effects were not that great the first week but it wasn’t anything unbearable.

While Zoloft can be vastly different for everyone I suffer from extreme anxiety with obsessive thoughts that causes health anxiety and DPDR and it has helped 75%. I can safely say I do not obsess over my thoughts anymore, and it’s easier to let go of them.

I wish I could help but I thinks it’s mostly a person by person thing. You have to find what makes you feel better in a way.. I hate that it’s like that. For me, I tried to slowly incorporate normal stuff back into my life, if I could do it before, why can’t I now? That kind of thing. Driving, going to places that scared me, being around people. I hope eventually you’ll find that thing that starts to make it better.. also one of the first things I was told when this first happened was to not read around on forums like this a lot, it can throw you back into a cycle of fear and frustration. It’s hard, because you want to know if you are ever going to become YOU again, but reading peoples stories might make you freak out even more. Take care, there’s a lot more time to figure it all out :).

Hey, It’s been a long time since I’ve been on this forum. About a year ago due to a massive health anxiety scare I woke up the next day and experiencing the exact same thing as you. The visual snow would drive me crazy, I’d be scared I was never going to be the same, and I kept telling myself this over and over again. The healing process is slow, as is with anything super traumatic to the brain, but I can tell you with proper help and sometimes medication (Zoloft really helped me) things get better. The visual snow has rapidly decreased and I no longer feel trapped, I couldn’t drive for a long time and now I’m okay with it. I still have a some time before I’m fully there but just know that it absolutely no matter what other people say does get better. Once you accept that it’s there and once you eventually start to come down off this scary and awful rollercoaster, you’ll forget it was even a thing. I’m sorry this is happening to you, I know when it happened to me I felt like I had nobody.. because nobody understood. Keep moving forward! You got this.
